newsitem.title: UK: Alpha Airport CEO to join Standard Chartered.
newsitem.headline: Alpha Airport CEO to join Standard Chartered.

text.p: Britain's Alpha Airports Group Plc, posting a rise in annual profits, said on Friday chief executive Paul Harrison planned to leave the company in the summer to join Standard Chartered Plc.
The airport services group said chairman Rodney Galpin would take on a more executive role until a successor was found for Harrison.
A Standard Chartered spokesman said Harrison would be group head of process and technology management and sit on the management team of the bank.
"He is expected to start at the beginning of July," the Standard spokesman said.
In addition to the management change, Alpha reported a 6.8 percent rise in pretax profits to 22.0 million stg before exceptionals for the year to January 31.
The company increased its final dividend to 3.50p per share, making a total dividend of 5.25p for the year versus 5.0p in 1995.
Alpha said its catering services division should benefit in 1997/98 from the elimination of U.S. losses after last year's sale of some flight catering kitchens.
The company also expected continued sales growth for its retail services business in all its markets, although margins were likely to remain at similar levels.
Alpha's shares slid 2.5p to 108.5 by 0915 GMT.
